newsitem.title: USA: Winston-Salem, N.C., rejects $75 mln GO package.
newsitem.headline: Winston-Salem, N.C., rejects $75 mln GO package.

text.p: Voters in Winston-Salem, North Carolina, overwhelmingly rejected five general obligation bond issues totalling $75 million, elections officials said Wednesday.
All five proposals failed by a margin of at least 2-1 in Tuesday's referendum.

The package included $47 million of GO bonds for street improvements, $11 million for housing and redevelopment, $7 million for renovations at the Benton Convention Center, $6 million for the purchase of land for economic development and $4 million for improvements at city parks and sports centers.
The bond proposal would have raised the city's property tax rate by 3 cents in 1998 and by another cent in 2000. The current rate is 52.5 cents per $100 of assessed value.
Opponents had complained that the tax rate hike would come on top of a recent revaluation that increased property assessments by an averages of 17 percent.
